intervention_label: DLL3 IHC (SP347) + PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 typing — diagnostic gate
expected_benefit: Not a therapy — resolves which antigen axes are open. DLL3 IHC gates the tarlatamab options; PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 typing together gate the entire PRAME class. Batchable on archival FFPE plus one blood tube, 1-3 week turnaround.
key_risks: None — diagnostic test on tissue and blood, non-toxic
A negative DLL3 IHC forecloses the BiTE options; a negative PRAME IHC or absent HLA-A*02:01 forecloses the ImmTAC/TCR-T class
preference_alignment: matches user 'prefers_trials': YES — this is the step that turns the RNA signal into an enrollable slot; costs 1-3 weeks before any antigen-directed option can start
guideline_status: NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 makes clinical-trial enrollment a preferred pathway for relapsed osteosarcoma; this workup is what tells you whether that pathway is open
rationale_summary: Every antigen-directed option below gates on protein-level confirmation the RNA signal cannot stand in for. DLL3 IHC (SP347, >=1% with >=25% preferred for stage-1 entry) opens the tarlatamab options; PRAME IHC plus HLA-A*02:01 typing together open the PRAME class. All five personas placed their entire ranking behind this step — it is non-toxic, archival tissue plus one blood tube cover it, and skipping it forecloses everything the patient nominated. HLA-A*02:01 prevalence runs ~40-50%, so roughly half of patients are ineligible for the whole PRAME class regardless of PRAME status. Batch all three tests day one rather than sequencing them.
open_questions: Whether SP347 assay availability at the treating institution is confirmed — not every reference lab carries the clone
Whether metastatic-site DLL3/PRAME expression diverges from the primary (spatial heterogeneity is a documented confounder)
likelihood_of_effect: N/A — diagnostic gate. Determines whether any downstream antigen-directed rec applies; PRAME axis more likely than not to hold, DLL3 protein status unknown.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic test on tissue and blood)

counter_productive_moa.description: Diagnostic gate, no mechanism of action

overall: The one move that unlocks the whole antigen list — cheap, archival, non-toxic; a negative result on either axis forecloses that half of the ranking.

intervention_label: tarlatamab (DLL3 x CD3 BiTE) via NCT06788938 (DLL3-IHC-gated basket)
scenario_label: If DLL3 IHC SP347 >=1% (preferably >=25% for stage-1 entry)
expected_benefit: Cross-tumor SCLC evidence only: DeLLphi-304 OS HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.47-0.77; median OS 13.6 vs 8.3 mo) and DeLLphi-301 ORR 40% (95% CI 29-52). No osteosarcoma efficacy data — the DLL3 IHC gate carries the extrapolation.
key_risks: CRS any-grade ~56%, G>=3 ~1% (DeLLphi-304); requires inpatient cycle-1 step-up dosing and CRS-mitigation protocol
G>=3 treatment-related AEs 24% (vs 53% on chemo comparator)
preference_alignment: matches user 'prefers_trials': YES; matches efficacy weight 0.85: PARTIAL — best-validated mechanism but efficacy is entirely SCLC-derived; no toxicity veto on file so CRS/ICANS burden does not violate a stated constraint
guideline_status: No consensus category in bone sarcoma; endorsed only under the NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 clinical-trial recommendation, not as a listed regimen
rationale_summary: Tarlatamab carries the only RCT-grade evidence on the board: DeLLphi-304 is a randomized phase 3 with a pre-specified OS primary that hit (HR 0.60, RoB2 Low), replicated in direction by the DeLLphi-301 ORR of 40%. The critic and conservative rank it first among the enrollable options because the mechanism is best-validated and the CRS/ICANS has a written step-up-plus-tocilizumab management algorithm, not because osteosarcoma benefit has been shown. The load-bearing gap is that every efficacy row is SCLC and the DLL3 signal here is RNA, not IHC-confirmed — the >=1% IHC gate (>=25% for stage-1 entry) does all the work and forecloses the option if negative. The risktaker would rank IMA203 above it on the 0.85 efficacy weight, arguing best-validated mechanism and best bet for this patient point in different directions; that is a ranking dissent, not a dissent on the drug, which stays on all five lists. DLL3 in osteosarcoma may be intracellular or below BiTE-killing density — RNA does not prove membrane localization.
open_questions: Whether osteosarcoma is confirmed on the NCT06788938 per-protocol enrolling list
Whether DLL3 protein reaches the membrane density a BiTE needs — the preclinical osteosarcoma data never measured surface protein
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate if DLL3 IHC confirms — best-validated mechanism (DeLLphi-304 OS HR 0.60) but efficacy is entirely SCLC-derived; no osteosarcoma data.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (CRS ~56% mostly G1-2, ICANS-like ~12%, G3+ TRAE 24%)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-mechanism CNS/neuro bystander activation and antigen-density-dependent escape if DLL3 membrane expression is low or heterogeneous

overall: The best-validated mechanism on the board and the lighter-toxicity DLL3 route — but every efficacy row is SCLC; osteosarcoma activity is a hypothesis until the IHC confirms surface target.

intervention_label: IMA203 (PRAME TCR-T) via NCT03686124 (ACTengine pan-solid basket, sarcoma cohort named)
expected_benefit: ORR 54% (95% CI 34-73) in the phase-1 pan-solid basket, median duration of response not reached at 9 months, mPFS 5.1 mo (Wermke et al., Nat Med 2025, n=28). Strongest efficacy signal in the dossier — but n=28, mixed histologies, no osteosarcoma-specific response reported.
key_risks: One treatment-related death from septic shock (1/28, 4%)
Universal G>=3 cytopenias after Cy/Flu lymphodepletion — a real immunosuppression window in a metastatic patient
preference_alignment: matches user 'prefers_trials': YES; matches efficacy weight 0.85 + 'accepts high-risk high-reward': YES on efficacy — highest ORR on the board with no toxicity veto on file; the septic death and lymphodepletion burden are surfaced but violate no stated constraint
guideline_status: No consensus category in osteosarcoma; guideline-consonant only under the NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025 clinical-trial recommendation
rationale_summary: This is the pick that lands squarely on the patient's PRAME axis with the biggest number in the dossier: ORR 54%, mDoR not reached, and the ACTengine basket names a sarcoma cohort outright rather than by cross-tumor argument. The risktaker and advocate lead it on the 0.85 efficacy weight and explicit high-risk appetite. Three personas dissented on ranking it high, honestly: the conservative and critic on the safety tail — one treatment-related septic death in n=28, CRS ~100% with G>=3 ~11%, ~25% ICANS, universal post-lymphodepletion cytopenias — and the critic further on imprecision, a 95% CI of 34-73 on 28 patients being a signal, not a rate to quote. The concensusite dissented on guideline fit: no consensus category, trial-enrollment pathway only. A death in a 28-person series is not a footnote, and the responders skewed melanoma, not bone — osteosarcoma-specific activity stays a hypothesis. Gated on PRAME IHC plus HLA-A*02:01, both unconfirmed; HLA-A*02:01 alone is a coin-flip on prevalence.
open_questions: Whether osteosarcoma contributes any response to the named sarcoma cohort — activity so far leans on synovial histology
Whether tumor HLA-LOH / B2M loss or a CD8-cold microenvironment would blunt durability even with PRAME and HLA both positive
likelihood_of_effect: High ceiling if both biomarkers confirm (ORR 54%, Nat Med 2025) but from n=28 with a wide CI and no osteosarcoma-specific responder; unstable point estimate.
toxicity_burden: High (1 treatment-related septic death; CRS ~100%/G3+ 11%, ICANS ~25%, universal G3+ cytopenias post-Cy/Flu)

counter_productive_moa.description: Antigen-loss / HLA-LOH escape and post-lymphodepletion immunosuppression window; durability unproven, responders melanoma-skewed

overall: The highest-response on-axis option with a named sarcoma cohort, and the one with a fatality on the board — efficacy-first personas lead it, three dissent on the safety tail and n=28 imprecision.

intervention_label: brenetafusp (IMC-F106C, PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC) via NCT04262466 / successor IMC-P115C
expected_benefit: Cross-tumor melanoma ImmTAC data: ORR 9-11% overall, but the PRAME-positive subset separates on mPFS (4.5 vs 2.1 mo) and 6-month OS (94% vs 40%). Off-the-shelf, no lymphodepletion. The subset OS figure is an unadjusted post-hoc split on an open-label phase-1 abstract — hypothesis-generating, not a survival claim.
key_risks: CRS ~85% any-grade but predominantly G1-2; no G>=3 CRS reported in the melanoma cohort
G>=3 TRAEs ~30%; manageable with dexamethasone pre-medication
preference_alignment: matches user 'prefers_trials': PARTIAL — the osteosarcoma-accepting basket cohort (NCT04262466) is active-not-recruiting and the NCI sarcoma trial (NCT07686367) enrolls synovial and myxoid/round-cell lipo, not bone; enrollability hinges on a re-opening or the IMC-P115C successor
guideline_status: No consensus category in osteosarcoma; trial-enrollment pathway only under NCCN Bone Cancer v2.2025
rationale_summary: The best-tolerated agent in the PRAME class, which is why the conservative ranks it above IMA203 despite weaker numbers: grade 1-2 CRS with zero G>=3 CRS in the melanoma cohort, no lymphodepletion, no marrow wipeout, AEs handled with dexamethasone pre-medication. The efficacy is genuinely modest — ORR 9-11%, overall mPFS 2.1 mo — with the durable benefit concentrated in a PRAME-positive responder subset that may or may not include osteosarcoma. The critic flags that the 6-month OS separation (94% vs 40%) is an unadjusted subgroup split on an open-label phase-1 ASCO 2024 abstract, not a peer-reviewed survival readout, and should not carry the weight of a survival claim across drugs and tumor types. It ranks above IMA203 on agreement_score because it draws no dissent, and below tarlatamab because the ImmTAC efficacy is thin and cross-tumor while tarlatamab carries RCT-grade mechanism evidence. Same PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 double gate as IMA203.
open_questions: Whether the sarcoma cohort re-opens or the IMC-P115C successor confirms osteosarcoma eligibility
Whether the PRAME-positive responder subset benefit extends to bone tumors — it is a melanoma-derived subgroup
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate: overall ORR 9-11%, benefit concentrated in a PRAME-positive subset (mPFS 4.5 vs 2.1 mo); melanoma-derived, cross-tumor.
toxicity_burden: Low (CRS predominantly G1-2, no G3+ CRS in cohort; rash ~70%, G3+ TRAE ~30%)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target/off-tumor rash and antigen-density dependence; dissent is enrollability-flavored, no mechanism-level counter-productive vector

overall: The best-tolerated PRAME route with an off-the-shelf, no-lymphodepletion trade — but modest single-agent efficacy and a sarcoma enrollment slot that is currently closed.

intervention_label: IMC-P115C (next-gen PRAME x CD3 ImmTAC) via NCT07156136
expected_benefit: No efficacy readout of its own — first-in-human dose-escalation. Buys the ImmTAC class and the PRAME target off brenetafusp's data; recruiting with pan-tumor PRAME-positive HLA-A*02:01-positive eligibility that admits non-melanoma histologies in principle.
key_risks: No IMC-P115C-specific safety data yet; class expectation is the brenetafusp CRS/rash profile (predominantly G1-2)
Sarcoma eligibility needs sponsor confirmation before it is a real slot
preference_alignment: matches user 'prefers_trials': YES — recruiting today where brenetafusp's sarcoma slot is closed; matches 'accepts high-risk high-reward': YES — buying the platform, not a number
guideline_status: No consensus category; trial-enrollment pathway only
rationale_summary: The open-door version of brenetafusp: a recruiting pan-tumor PRAME/HLA-A*02:01 basket where non-melanoma histologies are accepted in principle, so if brenetafusp's slot stays shut this is the ImmTAC a patient could enter today. As Immunocore's next-generation successor it is engineered off brenetafusp's data, which is the only reason to rank the mechanism — there is no human efficacy or safety readout for IMC-P115C itself. The critic's qualifier lands here too: the class OS figures borrowed from brenetafusp are an unadjusted phase-1 melanoma subset and should not be deployed as an IMC-P115C survival expectation. It ranks below brenetafusp because it is a pure platform bet with no data of its own, and above the registry-only options because it is actually recruiting. Same PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 gate.
open_questions: Whether sarcoma is on the per-protocol list — needs Immunocore medical-affairs confirmation
What the IMC-P115C dose-escalation safety and any early efficacy will show relative to brenetafusp
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown — first-in-human, no efficacy data; class bet on the ImmTAC platform and PRAME target, inferred from brenetafusp.
toxicity_burden: Low (no drug-specific data; class expectation predominantly G1-2 CRS and rash)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same on-target/off-tumor and antigen-density dependence as the ImmTAC class; no drug-specific counter-productive signal yet

overall: The recruiting-today PRAME ImmTAC when brenetafusp's sarcoma slot is closed — a platform-and-target bet with no efficacy readout of its own yet.

intervention_label: tarlatamab + radiation therapy via NCT06814496 (pan-tumor DLL3-IHC basket with RT)
expected_benefit: No combination efficacy or safety data — tier 5, registry-only, no results tab. Rationale rests on the abscopal hypothesis layered onto tarlatamab monotherapy efficacy (DeLLphi-301/304); the RT arm is a plausible way to push response depth in a metastatic patient with an irradiable site.
key_risks: No published combination AE profile; concurrent RT on a CRS/ICANS-prone BiTE is exactly the synergistic toxicity this phase 1 is designed to characterize
The BiTE component carries the tarlatamab class profile (CRS ~50% mostly G1-2, ICANS-like ~10%) plus site-specific radiation toxicity
preference_alignment: matches user 'prefers_trials': YES — a parallel DLL3 slot if the primary tarlatamab basket is full or out of reach; matches 'high-risk high-reward': PARTIAL — the incremental benefit over monotherapy is a hypothesis, not a finding
guideline_status: No consensus category; registry-only trial listing
rationale_summary: The monotherapy backbone here is the same well-characterized tarlatamab ranked at 2, and the pan-tumor DLL3-IHC gate could admit an IHC-positive osteosarcoma, with radiation layered on for an abscopal rationale. Both the conservative and the critic qualified rather than dissented: the reason to keep it low is specific and shared — there is no published AE profile for tarlatamab plus RT at all, and layering concurrent radiation onto a CRS/ICANS-prone BiTE is the kind of synergistic toxicity a dedicated combination trial has to characterize before anyone can quote a management algorithm. The monotherapy basket at rank 2 delivers the same backbone with a written step-up-and-tocilizumab protocol behind it, so this stays below it until the RT arm reports. It ranks below brenetafusp on the efficacy-toxicity tiebreak despite an equal agreement_score because brenetafusp has real phase-1 efficacy data while this combination has none. Same DLL3 IHC gate as rank 2; needs bone sarcoma confirmed on the enrolling list and an extracranial site amenable to radiation.
open_questions: Whether the RT-plus-BiTE combination toxicity is additive or synergistic — the primary phase-1 readout
Whether bone sarcoma is on the per-protocol histology list
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown — no combination data; abscopal benefit over tarlatamab monotherapy is a hypothesis the phase-1 is still measuring.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (uncharacterized combination; BiTE CRS ~50% mostly G1-2, ICANS-like ~10%, plus site-specific RT toxicity)

counter_productive_moa.description: Uncharacterized RT-on-BiTE synergistic toxicity; potential on-mechanism CNS/neuro bystander activation compounded by radiation

overall: A parallel DLL3 slot with an abscopal rationale — but zero combination data, and the monotherapy basket delivers the same backbone with a written safety algorithm.

intervention_label: NW-101C (PRAME TCR-T) via NCT07266298 (pan-solid PRAME/HLA-A*02:01 basket)
expected_benefit: None published — no NW-101C clinical data exist under that name. Efficacy expectation borrows entirely from the IMA203 PRAME TCR-T class precedent; pan-solid eligibility admits osteosarcoma in principle if both biomarkers confirm.
key_risks: No drug-specific safety data; class expectation is the IMA203 TCR-T profile — CRS, ICANS-like neurotoxicity, Cy/Flu lymphodepletion cytopenias
Registry-only; sarcoma acceptance needs sponsor confirmation
preference_alignment: matches user 'prefers_trials': YES — a redundant PRAME TCR-T slot if the IMA203 cohort is full or inaccessible; matches 'high-risk high-reward': PARTIAL — efficacy is inferred, not observed
guideline_status: No consensus category; registry-only trial listing
rationale_summary: A third PRAME-axis slot kept on the list for redundancy on the patient's own antigen: if the IMA203 cohort is full or geographically inaccessible, a second PRAME TCR-T program is a real fallback for a patient who accepts travel. It sits at the bottom for the reason the critic dissented on — there is no publication or abstract for NW-101C, the searchable name returns no clinical data, and keeping it ranked borrows its entire efficacy expectation from IMA203. Patient preference is a legitimate tie-breaker but cannot promote a tier-5 registry listing into a confident pick; it is named as a fallback slot to verify, not a lead. The toxicity will carry the same TCR-T lymphodepletion burden as IMA203 without any of its own data yet. Same PRAME IHC + HLA-A*02:01 gate.
open_questions: Whether NW-101C has any first-in-human safety or efficacy readout not yet indexed
Whether sarcoma is accepted on the per-protocol list
likelihood_of_effect: Unknown — no NW-101C data exist; efficacy inferred entirely from the IMA203 PRAME TCR-T class precedent.
toxicity_burden: High (no drug-specific data; class expectation is the IMA203 TCR-T profile — CRS, ICANS, post-lymphodepletion cytopenias)

counter_productive_moa.description: Same antigen-loss / HLA-LOH escape and lymphodepletion immunosuppression risk as the PRAME TCR-T class; no drug-specific data

overall: A redundant PRAME TCR-T fallback if the IMA203 slot is inaccessible — but zero data under this name; the efficacy expectation is entirely borrowed.
